title: Leaving McKinley, Goodman again, illness and Decca
summary: After two weeks with Benny in 1948, he did Decca work, then fell ill in 1950.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: How long did you stay with Ray then?
I have to think; a long time.

I think I got sick again in 1948 and while I was confined to bed and Benny called and wanted me to join him. I said I can't, I'm sick and he said, oh come on anyway. Meanwhile, I was still supposed to be doing things for Ray, but somehow he talked me into that and that let Ray off the hook. I never really went back after that; that was late '48. '49 I wasn't there any longer. Benny lasted about two weeks.

It just didn't work out. Then through '49 there wasn't very much there, except getting better. I got a chance to do some things for Decca Records, Gordon Jenkins, toward the end of '49. I thought I was going to get into the Decca crowd at that time, but that didn't work either. Then abruptly in '50 I got sick again.
What kind of things did you do for Decca?

Whatever they needed; vocals mostly. Gordon Jenkins was sort of a house man there. But that collapsed when I got sick and that went for a year, getting over it. Meanwhile, Bill had been sojourning and came back and Johnny Mercer got him to do a musical of his, 'Top Banana' and I was called in to help Bill.
